clauses.reason: Exhausted by performance on June 17, 1957, the date the order was signed. Its only operative words revoke Executive Order No. 9775 of September 3, 1946, which established the Federal Committee on Highway Safety, a one-time act that commands nothing afterwards. The order has no effective-date wording, so it is read as effective when signed; the Federal Register issue of June 19, 1957 is the alternative reading and is disclosed here. Actor: the order itself; the end source is its own operative text. The revoked order's non-operation is the surviving consequence, not a continuing command.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10715 (22 FR 4313, PDF pages 1-1; Federal Register issue of June 19, 1957; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10715.txt), headed Executive Order 10715, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on June 17, 1957. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Revoking Executive Order No. 9775 of September 3, 1946). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order has one operative sentence, the revocation of Executive Order No. 9775 of September 3, 1946, which established the Federal Committee on Highway Safety. The order states no effective date, so it took effect when signed on June 17, 1957; the Federal Register printed it on June 19, 1957, which is the alternative date a reader might take for effectiveness. The revocation is a single act that the order performs by its own words when it issues; once made it commands nothing further, so the clause is exhausted by performance on the signing date. What survives is the fact that the revoked order no longer operates, which is a consequence of the act and not a continuing command of this order. The three chosen machine searches state their coverage with no warning and their coverage notes were read. The U.S. Code and eCFR searches returned no hit for this order. The later-events search returned one hit, the Office of the Federal Register disposition note that this order revokes Executive Order 9775 and that the Federal Committee on Highway Safety is abolished; that note describes this order's own act, not a later event affecting this order (the machine status history carries the same note as a qualified-change flag, which I read and resolve the same way).
